quarterly_data.signal: Scale of the AI business put in a multi-year frame for the first time - CEO Adam Norvell: 'Our IT Data Comm business, which includes traditional IT Data Comm, and obviously a growing portion of AI specific, that business is FOUR TIMES THE SIZE IT WAS 2 YEARS AGO.' He attributes the disproportionate share of AI interconnect content to three things: breadth of products, depth/leadership across the technologies, and proven ability to execute on ramps - 'it wouldn't be so great if you're making racks that sell for $3 million and you can't deliver them to your customers because some connectors didn't show up on your dock.'
quarterly_data.figure: IT Datacom business four times the size it was 2 years ago

quarterly_data.signal: NEW disclosure on how AI customers are underwriting Amphenol's capacity - asked by the Citi moderator about NVIDIA publicly handing optical suppliers large sums to expand (the NVIDIA reference is the moderator's framing, not Amphenol's), the CEO said Amphenol does the same thing quietly: 'We work very closely with our customers. We get a lot of commitments from our customers. We also make zero announcements about it... we are working very intensively with our customers on making sure that to the extent that we make investments, that they are sharing in the risk of that, and they share in the risk of those investments in a variety of ways. That includes giving us LONG-TERM NON-CANCELLABLE ORDERS, which you could reframe as a big strategic agreement if you wanted to. It includes giving us PARTICIPATION IN INVESTMENTS when we make significant investments that are TAILOR-MADE FOR CERTAIN CUSTOMERS. We have had all of that happening, but in Amphenol, it is going to always happen in a very quiet fashion.' No customers named and no figures given.

Copper / optical / power split and the CommScope mix: 'Obviously, with CommScope, our optics position is more significant today, and we've talked about the fact that we now expect the CommScope acquisition, which when we bought it for $10.5 billion, we thought it would be a roughly $3.5 billion business. Now we expect it this year to be more than $4.5 billion in sales with higher margins and thereby better accretion. We've talked about the fact that MORE THAN THREE-QUARTERS OF THEIR BUSINESS IS OPTICS.' That puts Amphenol 'as one of the world leaders in optical interconnect,' while in power 'we are the leader in power interconnect' - a legacy of defense-market ultra-high voltage/power connectors, cable assemblies and busbars, where the risk is that 'you don't want to catch a $3 million GPU rack on fire.' High-speed copper remains a big piece, with good balance across all three.
quarterly_data.figure: CommScope bought for $10.5 billion, originally seen as roughly $3.5 billion of sales, now more than $4.5 billion this year; more than three-quarters of CommScope's business is optics
